newsitem.title: UK: UK plans paedophile register in crime crackdown.
newsitem.headline: UK plans paedophile register in crime crackdown.

text.p: Britain's interior minister unveiled plans on Tuesday for a register of paedophiles and other sex offenders as part of a major crime crackdown plan he will present to parliament within weeks.

Michael Howard won a standing ovation from delegates to the ruling Conservative Party conference for a speech in which he also promised to bring in automatic life sentences for repeat offenders committing crimes such as murder and rape.

"I believe a register of paedophiles is needed. It's the best way to keep track of them. The police have asked for it, our children need it and I intend to bring it in," Home Secretary Howard told the conference.

Government sources said convicted sex offenders would be obliged to tell the police of any change of address upon release. It would also be made a criminal offence for convicted sex offenders to take a job involving access to children.
Opinion polls show crime is a major concern for voters ahead of the next general election, which must be held by May 1997.

The Conservatives traditionally portray themselves as the party of law and order but government figures last month showed that crime had risen in England and Wales for the first time in two years, with the biggest increase in violent crimes.

In a lengthy list of pledges, Howard promised to give local councils the power to close night clubs if a senior policeman said drug dealing was taking place there and to bring in a new automatic minimum seven-year jail sentence for dealing.
All adults who committed a second offence of murder, attempted murder, wounding, robbery with firearms, rape or sex with a girl under 13 would automatically get a life sentence.
Howard pledged to crack down on under-age drinking, giving police the power to seize alcohol from anyone under 18 found drinking in a public place.
